options.label: Yes, archive all 3
options.description: I dry-run first, then `sessions archive cse_01Ehv4f28o… cse_01KF1mj5z… cse_011HRta…`. Picker drops 3 stale rows. Reversible — they re-appear under `sessions list --all`. Recommended.

options.description: A is the oldest (#5 label flip) and has the worst-looking dup'd title — some might argue it's the strongest case for archiving. Picking this just means you want to keep A for some reason.

options.label: Skip — leave them all
options.description: Picker stays cluttered. Risk: more stale rows accumulate as Worker C closes.

questions.question: Update the manage skill to auto-archive after `close` (and optionally `forget`)?

options.label: Auto-archive on close only
options.description: After `workers.sh close`, run `sessions archive` for the worker. Forget'd workers stay live (boss may want to revisit them). Cleanest default. Recommended.

options.label: Auto-archive on close AND forget
options.description: Both teardown paths archive. Forget'd workers also disappear from picker. Stronger cleanup, but you'd lose the visual cue that you intentionally walked away from one.

options.label: Don't auto-archive — keep it manual
options.description: Archive only when you explicitly ask. Leaves the cleanup discretionary.
